items.title: Etale ring maps preserve the dimension of localisations at corresponding primes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that an etale ring map preserves the dimension of the localisations at a prime and a prime above it. The proof establishes the two inequalities separately: flatness gives going down, hence the dimension of the source localisation is at most that of the target; and any chain of primes in the target localisation maps to a chain of primes in the source localisation, which is strictly increasing because an etale map is quasi-finite and a quasi-finite map has discrete fibres on spectra, giving the reverse inequality. Both inequalities are argued directly from the cited properties.
